from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Dimensions define our degrees of spatial freedom.", "A 2D Flatlander cannot perceive 3D depth.", "We appear strange to lower-dimensional beings."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Flatlander Paradox", lecture_lines)
        
        # 0D Point
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        label_dot = Text("Point", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'B2')
        label_dot.next_to(dot, DOWN)
        
        # 1D Line
        line = Line(start=self.grid['B3'], end=self.grid['B5'], color="#FF00FF")
        label_line = Text("Line", color="#FF00FF", font_size=20)
        label_line.next_to(line, DOWN)
        
        # 2D Square
        square = Square(side_length=1, color="#00FFFF")
        label_square = Text("Square", color="#00FFFF", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'E2')
        label_square.next_to(square, DOWN)
        
        # 3D Cube
        cube = Cube(side_length=1, fill_opacity=0.5, color="#FFFF00")
        label_cube = Text("Cube", color="#FFFF00", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(cube, 'E5')
        label_cube.next_to(cube, DOWN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF99"))
        self.play(Create(dot), Write(label_dot))
        self.play(Create(line), Write(label_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#99FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(square), Write(label_square))
        self.play(Rotate(square, angle=PI/4))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF99FF"))
        self.play(Create(cube), Write(label_cube))
        self.play(Rotate(cube, angle=PI/4, axis=UP + RIGHT))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Apply the sweep method to a 3D cube.",
            "Dragging it creates a 4D Tesseract.",
            "We visualize 4D objects through their shadows.",
            "The shadow projects into our 3D space.",
            "Complexity grows with every added spatial dimension."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Leap to 4D: The Tesseract", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        sq = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(sq, "C3")
        self.play(Create(sq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        sq2 = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE).shift(UP * 0.3 + RIGHT * 0.3)
        self.play(Create(sq2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        tesseract = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_color="#FF00FF").rotate(PI/6, axis=RIGHT+UP)
        self.place_at_grid(tesseract, "C3")
        self.play(Transform(VGroup(sq, sq2), tesseract))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Rotate(tesseract, angle=TAU/4, axis=UP))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(BLUE)
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=p, color="#00FFFF") for p in tesseract.get_all_points()])
        self.play(Flash(dots, color="#00FFFF", run_time=2))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Escape Puzzle", [
            "Can a 2D creature escape a locked room?", 
            "Yes, by jumping into the third dimension.", 
            "A 4D entity similarly bypasses 3D barriers."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        room = Square(color=RED, side_length=2.5)
        creature = Dot(color=YELLOW, radius=0.15)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(room, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(room))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(creature, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(creature))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move creature out "up"
        self.play(
            creature.animate.shift(UP * 3),
            FadeOut(creature)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        ghost = Dot(color=BLUE, radius=0.15)
        self.place_at_grid(ghost, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(ghost))
        self.play(ghost.animate.shift(UP * 2 + RIGHT * 2).set_opacity(0.3))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Dimensional shifts change our perspective on space.",
            "Advanced geometry adds new spatial constraints.",
            "Everything connects through mathematical projection."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Summary and Perspective", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # 1. Dimensional shift cube visuals
        cube_4d = Cube(fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2, color=BLUE).scale(0.8)
        cube_3d = Cube(fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2, color=GREEN).scale(0.5)
        square_2d = Square(fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2, color=YELLOW).scale(0.4)
        
        self.place_in_area(cube_4d, 'A2', 'C4')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(cube_4d))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]), run_time=1)
        self.play(Transform(cube_4d, cube_3d))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]), run_time=1)
        self.play(Transform(cube_4d, square_2d))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.target_audience: High school students interested in STEM

sections.title: Introduction: The Flatlander Paradox
sections.content: Establish prerequisite knowledge by defining a 'dimension' as a degree of freedom. Introduce the concept of a 2D entity (Flatlander) unable to perceive depth, to help students conceptualize how we (3D beings) might look to a 4D entity.
sections.example: An animation showing a square moving through a 2D line, vs. a sphere passing through a 2D plane appearing as a circle that grows and shrinks.

sections.title: Mapping Dimensions: 1D to 2D to 3D
sections.content: Teach the 'sweep' method: Drag a point to create a line (1D), drag a line to create a square (2D), drag a square to create a cube (3D). Define vertices and edges as the building blocks for extrapolation.
sections.example: Visual transition: A dot (0D) → A segment (1D) → A square (2D) → A cube (3D), highlighting how each step introduces one new axis.

sections.title: The Leap to 4D: The Tesseract
sections.content: Apply the 'sweep' method to the 3D cube. By dragging a 3D cube along an invisible 'w' axis, we visualize the Tesseract (hypercube). Explain that while we can't 'see' 4D, we can project its 'shadow' into our 3D space.
sections.example: An animation of a rotating Tesseract 'shadow'—a cube-within-a-cube where lines seem to pass through each other, demonstrating the spatial complexity of a 4D object.

sections.title: Application: The Escape Puzzle
sections.content: Challenge the students with a dimensional puzzle: How would a 2D creature escape a locked 2D square room? (By 'jumping' into the 3rd dimension). Analogize this to how a 4D entity could bypass any 3D physical barrier.
sections.example: A cartoon '2D Cat' trapped in a drawn square on paper, suddenly vanishing by moving 'up' into the 3D space, demonstrating dimensional escape.

sections.title: Conclusion: Summary and Perspective
sections.content: Recap that dimensional shifting is about changing perspective. Emphasize that advanced geometry is essentially the study of how structures behave when we add a new spatial constraint.
sections.example: A final visual of a 4D object collapsing back into a 3D cube, then a 2D square, reinforcing the concept of mathematical projection.
